newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens can't confirm China dam report.
newsitem.headline: Siemens can't confirm China dam report.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG said on Friday it could not confirm reports it had won contracts to supply turbines and generators for China's massive Three Gorges dam project.
"We have seen the reports, but I can't confirm them," a spokeswoman for Siemens's power generation unit (KWU) told Reuters. "We have received no final decision from the Chinese government."
An official from the project headquarters in central China also told Reuters a final decision had not been made.

Reports from Beijing, quoting unnamed "informed business sources", said an alliance of Siemens, Germany's J.M. Voith and a Canadian subsidiary of GE Co. of the U.S. were chosen to supply six turbines and six generators for the project.
British-French concern GEC Alsthom would provide eight turbines and Swiss-Swedish group Asea Brown Boveri Ltd would provide eight generators, they said.
The total value of the contracts was expected to be around $800 million. Started in 1993, the Three Gorges dam is the world's largest water project and involves 14 generating units.
Westinghouse Canada, Impsa of Argentina, as well as a Russian consortium and a Japanese alliance were also bidding on the contracts.
